items.explanation: Early arrival creates the opportunity. Confirmation comes before the described use of the ticket.

items.title: A ticket machine
items.context:
A. The machine printed the ticket after the payment.
B. I paid the displayed amount by card.
C. The machine displayed the fare.
D. I selected my destination on the ticket machine.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → C → B → A
C → D → B → A
D → B → C → A
D → C → A → B
items.explanation: The destination determines the fare. Printing is explicitly placed after payment.

items.title: A road closure
items.context:
A. Our usual road was blocked when we reached the junction.
B. We stopped and checked the diversion sign.
C. We took that road and rejoined our route beyond the closure.
D. It directed us along the river road.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → A → D → C
A → D → B → C
A → B → C → D
A → B → D → C
items.explanation: The blocked road prompts a check. The alternative route is identified before it is taken.

items.title: Checking a suitcase
items.context:
A. At the airport counter, I placed my suitcase on the scale.
B. She then put the labelled suitcase on the belt.
C. After it moved away, she gave me the baggage receipt.
D. The assistant weighed it and attached a label.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → B → C
D → A → B → C
A → B → D → C
A → D → C → B
items.explanation: The suitcase is labelled before being put on the belt. The receipt is given after it moves away.

items.title: Finding the right stop
items.context:
A. I showed the driver the address.
B. I boarded the bus but did not know which stop I needed.
C. I watched for that name and got off there.
D. The driver told me the stop name.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → A → C → D
B → A → D → C
A → B → D → C
B → D → A → C
items.explanation: The address helps the driver identify the stop. The traveller learns the name before watching for it.

items.title: A shared taxi
items.context:
A. The last bus was cancelled while several of us were waiting.
B. One passenger called a taxi for the group.
C. When it arrived, we all got in.
D. We agreed to share a taxi instead.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → B → C
A → B → D → C
A → D → C → B
A → D → B → C
items.explanation: The cancellation causes the new plan. Agreement and booking precede the taxi’s arrival.

items.title: Correcting a message
items.context:
A. I sent a message with the wrong meeting time.
B. The recipient replied to confirm the new time.
C. I noticed the mistake after sending it.
D. I sent a second message with the correct time.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → D → B
C → A → D → B
A → D → C → B
A → C → B → D
items.explanation: The first message must be sent before its mistake is noticed afterward. Confirmation follows the correction.

items.title: Preparing a presentation
items.context:
A. I chose a topic for my short presentation.
B. After practising, I gave the presentation to the group.
C. I made notes about that topic.
D. Using the notes, I practised explaining it aloud.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → A → D → B
A → D → C → B
A → C → B → D
A → C → D → B
items.explanation: The topic guides the notes. The notes support practice, which comes before the presentation.

items.title: An unfamiliar word
items.context:
A. I checked its meaning in a dictionary.
B. I found a word I did not understand in an article.
C. The sentence made sense on my second reading.
D. I reread the sentence using that meaning.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → B → D → C
B → D → A → C
B → A → C → D
B → A → D → C
items.explanation: The unknown word prompts the dictionary check. The new meaning is used in the second reading.

items.title: A revised paragraph
items.context:
A. I gave my first paragraph to the teacher.
B. The teacher marked two places that were unclear.
C. I submitted the revised paragraph.
D. I rewrote those two places.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → B → C
A → B → C → D
A → B → D → C
B → A → D → C
items.explanation: The marked feedback identifies what to rewrite. The revised version is submitted after rewriting.

items.title: Sending an attachment
items.context:
A. Before sending it, I noticed that no file was attached.
B. I wrote an email saying that a file was attached.
C. I added the missing file.
D. I sent the email with the attachment.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → A → D → C
B → A → C → D
A → B → C → D
B → C → A → D
items.explanation: The missing attachment is noticed before sending. It is added before the final email goes out.

items.title: Joining an online class
items.context:
A. A message asked me to enter my name.
B. The class window opened after I joined.
C. I entered my name and clicked “Join.”
D. I opened the class link on my computer.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → B → C
D → A → C → B
A → D → C → B
D → C → A → B
items.explanation: The link opens the entry process. Entering the name and joining precede the class window.

items.title: A study reminder
items.context:
A. I set a reminder for the planned study time.
B. The reminder appeared while I was reading.
C. I paused my reading and reviewed the words.
D. I planned to review five words that evening.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → B → C
D → B → A → C
D → A → C → B
D → A → B → C
items.explanation: The planned study time comes before the reminder. The reminder causes the switch from reading to review.

items.title: Finding a document
items.context:
A. I opened the copy found by the search.
B. The search showed it in the Downloads folder.
C. I searched the computer using its title.
D. I could not find the document in my usual folder.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → D → B → A
D → B → C → A
D → C → A → B
D → C → B → A
items.explanation: The search produces the location. The located copy is opened afterward.

items.title: Clarifying homework
items.context:
A. She replied that only the first four were required.
B. I asked the teacher to confirm the number.
C. I read the homework instructions but was unsure how many questions to answer.
D. I completed those four questions.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → B → A → D
B → C → A → D
C → A → B → D
C → B → D → A
items.explanation: The unclear instruction leads to a question. The reply identifies the four questions then completed.

items.title: A pronunciation note
items.context:
A. At the next lesson, I showed the list to my teacher.
B. I wrote the word on my Questions list.
C. We practised the word together.
D. During practice, I noticed a word that was hard for me to say.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → B → A → C
B → D → A → C
D → A → B → C
D → B → C → A
items.explanation: The difficulty is recorded before the later lesson. Showing the list leads to the practice.

items.title: A room booking
items.context:
A. We chose a date for the workshop.
B. I booked one of the available rooms.
C. I sent everyone the confirmed date and room.
D. I checked which rooms were available on that date.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → B → C
A → B → D → C
A → D → C → B
A → D → B → C
items.explanation: The date guides the availability check. The room must be booked before its confirmation is sent.

items.title: An updated schedule
items.context:
A. A speaker told us she could arrive only after two.
B. I updated the schedule with the new time.
C. We moved her talk from one o’clock to three.
D. I sent the updated schedule to the guests.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → B → D
C → A → B → D
A → B → C → D
A → C → D → B
items.explanation: The arrival restriction causes the change. The schedule is updated before that version is sent.

items.title: Checking an order
items.context:
A. The delivery arrived with three sealed boxes.
B. I found that one item was missing.
C. I opened them and compared the contents with our order.
D. I contacted the supplier about the missing item.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → B → D
C → A → B → D
A → B → C → D
A → C → D → B
items.explanation: The boxes must be opened before their contents can be checked. The specific problem is found before it is reported.

items.title: A clearer instruction
items.context:
A. She asked which file I meant and when I needed it.
B. I named the file and gave a deadline of four o’clock.
C. I asked a colleague to “send it soon.”
D. She sent that file before four.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → A → D → B
C → A → B → D
A → C → B → D
C → B → A → D
items.explanation: The vague request triggers clarification. The precise file and time are supplied before the completed task.

items.title: Testing a new form
items.context:
A. We rewrote that question before publishing the form.
B. Two colleagues tried filling in the draft.
C. We made a draft of the new registration form.
D. Their comments showed that one question was unclear.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → B → A → D
C → B → D → A
B → C → D → A
C → D → B → A
items.explanation: The draft is needed for testing. Test comments identify the question that is rewritten.

items.title: A delayed payment
items.context:
A. The customer found a wrong digit in the reference.
B. I asked the customer to check the payment reference.
C. They corrected it, and the payment was then matched to our invoice.
D. I noticed that a payment had not appeared in our account.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → B → C → A
D → B → A → C
B → D → A → C
D → A → B → C
items.explanation: The missing payment prompts the check. Finding the wrong digit precedes correcting it and matching the payment.

items.title: An unsuitable meeting time
items.context:
A. One colleague said she would still be travelling then.
B. She confirmed that the later time worked.
C. I proposed ten-thirty instead.
D. I suggested a meeting at nine.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → C → A → B
D → A → B → C
D → A → C → B
A → D → C → B
items.explanation: The travel conflict responds to the first suggestion. The later proposal is confirmed only after it is made.

items.title: A printer queue
items.context:
A. I asked the owner to clear it, and my document printed afterward.
B. Nothing printed, so I checked the print queue.
C. I sent a document to the shared printer.
D. The queue showed a paused job ahead of mine.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → D → B → A
C → B → A → D
C → B → D → A
B → C → D → A
items.explanation: The failed print leads to checking the queue. The blockage is found and cleared before printing succeeds.

items.title: Confirming a decision
items.context:
A. The group chose the middle date.
B. We discussed three possible dates for the visit.
C. I repeated the chosen date to check that everyone agreed.
D. After everyone confirmed it, I made the booking.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → C → A → D
B → A → D → C
B → A → C → D
A → B → C → D
items.explanation: Discussion comes before selection. The booking follows explicit confirmation of the selected date.

items.title: A revised estimate
items.context:
A. A customer asked us to include an extra room in the job.
B. The customer accepted that estimate before we began.
C. I sent a revised estimate showing the new total.
D. I calculated the extra work and cost.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → D → B
A → D → B → C
A → D → C → B
D → A → C → B
items.explanation: The extra request causes recalculation. Acceptance refers to the revised estimate already sent.

items.title: A wrong parcel
items.context:
A. The item numbers were different, so I contacted the seller.
B. The seller used those numbers to arrange the correct replacement.
C. I compared its label with my order confirmation.
D. I opened the parcel and found an item I had not ordered.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → C → B
D → C → B → A
D → C → A → B
C → D → A → B
items.explanation: Opening reveals the problem. The comparison supplies the evidence used in the contact and replacement.

items.title: A leaking bottle
items.context:
A. Water appeared at the bottom of my bag.
B. I tightened the lid and dried the bag.
C. I checked again later, and no more water had leaked.
D. I checked the bottle inside and found its lid loose.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → B → D → C
A → D → C → B
A → D → B → C
D → A → B → C
items.explanation: The water prompts inspection. Finding the loose lid leads to tightening it, followed by a check of the result.

items.title: A locked account
items.context:
A. The email arrived with a link to choose a new password.
B. My sign-in attempt was rejected.
C. I used the password-reset link to request an email.
D. I set a new password through that link and signed in.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → C → A → D
C → B → A → D
B → A → C → D
B → C → D → A
items.explanation: The failed sign-in starts the reset. The email link must arrive before it can be used.

items.title: A blurred scan
items.context:
A. I scanned the form and checked the result.
B. The text in the second scan was clear enough to send.
C. The small print was too blurred to read.
D. I made a second scan at a higher quality.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → C → B
A → C → B → D
A → C → D → B
C → A → D → B
items.explanation: The first scan is inspected before its problem is identified. The second scan follows the quality change.

items.title: A noisy room
items.context:
A. Our group could not hear the speaker over the noise outside.
B. The receptionist offered an empty room at the back.
C. We asked whether a quieter room was free.
D. We moved there and continued the discussion.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → B → D
C → A → B → D
A → B → C → D
A → C → D → B
items.explanation: The noise creates the need for a room. The available alternative is identified before the move.

items.title: A duplicate reservation
items.context:
A. They cancelled the duplicate and confirmed the remaining reservation.
B. I checked the booking numbers and saw that they were different.
C. I contacted the venue and explained that I needed only one booking.
D. I received two confirmation emails for the same visit.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → B → A → C
D → B → C → A
B → D → C → A
D → C → B → A
items.explanation: Two emails prompt a comparison. Different booking numbers establish the duplicate that is then cancelled.

items.title: A missing page
items.context:
A. The page numbers jumped from four to six.
B. I inserted it between pages four and six.
C. I checked the printed report before the meeting.
D. I printed the missing page five.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → D → B
C → D → A → B
C → A → B → D
C → A → D → B
items.explanation: Checking reveals the numbering gap. Page five is printed before it can be inserted.

items.title: A file that would not open
items.context:
A. The replacement file opened successfully.
B. I told the sender which error message I saw.
C. The sender converted the file to a different format.
D. The file would not open on my computer.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → D → C → A
D → C → B → A
D → B → A → C
D → B → C → A
items.explanation: The opening problem leads to reporting the error. Conversion produces the replacement that then works.

items.title: A price difference
items.context:
A. She checked the product code in the photo.
B. She corrected the checkout price after confirming the match.
C. At the checkout, the price was higher than the shelf label.
D. I showed the assistant a photo of the label.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → D → A → B
D → C → A → B
C → A → D → B
C → D → B → A
items.explanation: The price difference prompts evidence. The code is checked before the described correction.

items.title: A lost connection
items.context:
A. The call disconnected in the middle of an explanation.
B. Once we were connected again, I said which part I had missed.
C. They repeated that part, and we continued.
D. I called the person back.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → C → B
A → D → B → C
D → A → B → C
A → B → D → C
items.explanation: Reconnection is necessary before the missing part can be discussed and repeated.

items.title: A moved outdoor event
items.context:
A. We notified guests of the new indoor location.
B. We checked whether the indoor hall was free.
C. Rain was forecast for the afternoon of our outdoor event.
D. The hall was available, so we moved the event there.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: C → D → B → A
C → B → A → D
C → B → D → A
B → C → D → A
items.explanation: The forecast motivates checking an alternative. Availability allows the move, which must precede notification of the new location.

items.title: A changed plan
items.context:
A. A notice said that train would not run that day.
B. I chose the bus because it would arrive earlier than the train alternative.
C. I compared the bus with a route using two other trains.
D. I planned to take the direct train.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → C → B
D → C → A → B
D → A → B → C
D → A → C → B
items.explanation: The cancellation forces a comparison. The choice is based on that comparison.

items.title: An extra example
items.context:
A. I asked which part was unclear.
B. She said she did not understand the final step.
C. I demonstrated that step with a new example.
D. I explained the instruction, but the learner still looked uncertain.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → C → B
D → A → B → C
A → D → B → C
D → B → A → C
items.explanation: The uncertainty prompts a specific question. Its answer identifies the step to demonstrate.

items.title: A better seat
items.context:
A. I asked the attendant whether I could move.
B. He pointed out an empty seat with a clear view.
C. From my seat, a pillar blocked part of the screen.
D. I moved to that seat and could see the whole screen.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → B → D
C → B → A → D
C → A → D → B
C → A → B → D
items.explanation: The blocked view motivates the request. The identified alternative is used afterward.

items.title: A late reply
items.context:
A. I checked the original message and found a typing error in the address.
B. I corrected the address and sent the question again.
C. This time the office received it and answered.
D. I sent a question to the office and waited two days without a reply.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → B → C
D → B → A → C
D → A → C → B
D → A → B → C
items.explanation: The lack of reply leads to checking the address. Correcting it explains why the second message reaches the office.

items.title: A clearer explanation
items.context:
A. I asked permission to start again with the main point.
B. She then described the idea correctly in her own words.
C. After she agreed, I gave one short explanation and an example.
D. The customer could not follow my long explanation.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → C → B
A → D → C → B
D → C → A → B
D → A → B → C
items.explanation: The first explanation fails. Permission precedes the simpler explanation, and the customer’s response shows its result.

items.title: Planning enough time
items.context:
A. My first trip to the office took longer than I expected.
B. That change allowed me to arrive before the appointment.
C. For the next trip, I chose an earlier connecting service.
D. I noted which connection had caused the delay.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → D → C → B
D → A → C → B
A → C → D → B
A → D → B → C
items.explanation: The first delay provides information for the revised plan. The later arrival is the result of that change.

items.title: A useful correction
items.context:
A. I corrected my directions before the visitor left.
B. The visitor thanked us and went to the second floor.
C. A colleague quietly reminded me that it had moved to the second floor.
D. I told the visitor that the room was on the third floor.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: D → A → C → B
D → C → B → A
D → C → A → B
C → D → A → B
items.explanation: The reminder corrects the first information. The revised directions must come before the visitor follows them.

items.title: Choosing a suitable size
items.context:
A. I chose a box smaller than the available space.
B. I measured the shelf space before ordering a storage box.
C. When it arrived, it fitted on the shelf.
D. I compared those measurements with the sizes on the website.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: B → D → C → A
B → D → A → C
D → B → A → C
B → A → D → C
items.explanation: The measurements support the comparison and choice. The fit can be checked after the chosen box arrives.

items.title: Checking the whole message
items.context:
A. I received a message saying the appointment time had changed.
B. I reached the new building at the new time.
C. Before leaving, I read the rest of the message.
D. It also named a different building, so I changed my route.
items.prompt: Which order tells the story clearly from start to finish?
options: A → C → D → B
C → A → D → B
A → D → C → B
A → C → B → D
items.explanation: Reading the full message reveals a second change. The route must change before arrival at the new building.

activities.name: Missing Details
activities.description: Choose what to ask when useful information is missing.

items.context: Your appointment is at 10:00 on Tuesday. The message gives the street address but no room number.
items.prompt: Which question fills the gap you need on arrival?
options: What day is the appointment?
What time does the appointment start?
What is the street address?
Which room should I go to?
items.explanation: The date, time, and address are already known. The room is the missing detail.
items.reply: Please go to room 204 on the second floor.

items.context: A workshop starts at 14:00 and lasts two hours. You have the venue address but no date.
items.prompt: What must you ask before putting it in your calendar?
options: On which date is the workshop?
How long does the workshop last?
What time does the workshop start?
Where is the venue?
items.explanation: A start time without a date is not enough to schedule the visit.
items.reply: It is on 18 November.

items.context: You have a booking for two people at 19:00. You need to change it to 20:00.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether the change is possible?
options: What time is my current booking?
Can you confirm that you received my original booking?
Is a table for two available at 20:00?
How many people is my current booking for?
items.explanation: The number of guests and current time are known. Availability at the proposed new time is the needed fact.
items.reply: Yes, we can move your booking to 20:00.

items.context: You will arrive at a guesthouse at 22:00. Check-in begins at 15:00, but no closing time is listed.
items.prompt: Which detail should you request?
options: How many rooms does the guesthouse have?
Can I check in at 22:00?
Does check-in begin at 15:00?
What time does breakfast start?
items.explanation: The start of check-in does not establish whether late arrival is possible.
items.reply: Yes. Use the side-door keypad after 21:00; we will send the code privately.

items.context: Your visitor pass is ready. The email says to bring identification but does not say which kinds it accepts.
items.prompt: Which question checks the requirement?
options: Is my visitor pass ready?
Should I bring identification?
Do I need to print the pass or show it on my phone?
Which forms of identification do you accept?
items.explanation: You already know identification is required. You need to know which document qualifies.
items.reply: A passport or a government-issued photo card is accepted.

items.context: An exhibition ticket is valid all day. You want to leave for lunch and return afterward.
items.prompt: What should you ask?
options: Can I lend this ticket to another visitor?
Can I use this ticket on a different day?
Can I visit every part of the exhibition with this ticket?
Can I leave and re-enter with this ticket?
items.explanation: All-day validity does not automatically tell you the re-entry policy.
items.reply: Yes. Keep your ticket and show it when you return.

items.context: You know the meeting date and time. The invitation says “Main building,” but the campus has several entrances.
items.prompt: Which question helps you enter the correct place?
options: What time should I arrive for the meeting?
Which entrance should I use?
How long should I allow for the meeting?
Which building is the meeting in?
items.explanation: The entrance is the missing navigation detail. The other facts do not identify where to enter.
items.reply: Use the east entrance beside the bicycle racks.

items.context: You have booked a walking tour. The start time and meeting point are clear, but you have another appointment later.
items.prompt: What do you need to ask to plan the rest of your day?
options: What time does the tour finish?
Where does the tour start?
What time does the tour start?
How much walking does the tour involve?
items.explanation: The finishing time determines whether the tour fits before your next appointment.
items.reply: The tour finishes at about 12:30 at the same meeting point.

items.context: A class requires registration. You know how to register but not the latest date for doing so.
items.prompt: Which question asks for the missing limit?
options: How will I receive confirmation after registering?
What is the registration deadline?
How do I register?
Is registration required?
items.explanation: The deadline tells you how long you have to act. The method is already known.
items.reply: Please register by 17:00 on Friday.

items.context: You have reserved a meeting room for an hour. You need to set up the room before your guests arrive.
items.prompt: Which question helps you plan the setup?
options: Can I change the number of guests on my booking?
Can I cancel the room without a fee?
Can I enter the room before the booking starts?
Can I extend the room booking by an hour?
items.explanation: The reservation length does not tell you whether early access is allowed.
items.reply: You may enter ten minutes before your booked start time.

items.context: Your train arrives at 16:20. A shuttle runs from the station to the hotel, but its timetable is missing.
items.prompt: Which question helps you choose a shuttle?
options: What time does my train arrive?
When is the first shuttle after 16:20?
How often does the train run?
Does the shuttle go to the hotel?
items.explanation: You know the destination and arrival time. You need the next usable shuttle departure.
items.reply: The next shuttle leaves at 16:40 from stop B.

items.context: You must collect a parcel today. You know the counter’s address, but not when it closes.
items.prompt: What should you ask before travelling?
options: Can someone else collect the parcel for me?
What time does the collection counter close today?
What is the counter’s address?
How will I know the parcel is ready?
items.explanation: Today’s closing time determines whether you can still collect the parcel.
items.reply: The counter closes at 18:00 today.

items.context: A bus ticket covers one journey. You need to change buses halfway to your destination.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether this ticket is enough?
options: Does this ticket allow a transfer to the second bus?
Can I use this ticket again on the return journey?
Can I buy this ticket from the driver?
Can I use this ticket on a different day?
items.explanation: A journey ticket may or may not include transfers. Check the policy instead of assuming.
items.reply: Yes. One transfer is included within ninety minutes of the first boarding.

items.context: You booked a rental bicycle for Saturday. The confirmation gives the pickup point but no return point.
items.prompt: Which question fills that gap?
options: How many gears does the bicycle have?
Where should I return the bicycle?
Where should I collect the bicycle?
What day is my booking?
items.explanation: Pickup and return locations need not be the same. The return location is not yet known.
items.reply: Return it to the same desk where you collect it.

items.context: Your ticket is for the 09:00 coach. You may arrive early enough for the 08:30 coach.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether you may use the earlier service?
options: Can I get a refund if I miss both coaches?
Is my ticket valid on the 08:30 coach?
Can I change my seat on the 09:00 coach?
Can I bring a second bag on the coach?
items.explanation: Being early does not establish ticket validity on a different departure.
items.reply: No. This ticket is valid only on the booked departure.

items.context: You need to take a bicycle on a train. The route and departure time are known.
items.prompt: What must you check about the bicycle?
options: What time does the train leave?
Do I need to change trains on this route?
Do I need a separate bicycle reservation?
Which route does the train follow?
items.explanation: The missing rule concerns taking a bicycle, not the already known route or time.
items.reply: Yes. Bicycle spaces must be reserved before travel.

items.context: You will collect equipment using a small car. The package is listed as one box, but its size is not given.
items.prompt: Which question helps you check whether it will fit?
options: What are the packed box dimensions?
How much does the box weigh?
How many boxes are there?
Is the equipment assembled inside the box?
items.explanation: One box could be small or large. Its dimensions are needed to compare it with the car’s space.
items.reply: The packed box is 80 by 50 by 40 centimetres.

items.context: A museum is a short walk from the station. You are bringing a suitcase and do not want to carry it through the galleries.
items.prompt: Which question addresses your need?
options: Can I use a different entrance to the galleries?
Is there a place to store a suitcase?
Can I leave and re-enter the museum?
Can I buy a ticket at the entrance?
items.explanation: Your problem is storing luggage during the visit. Distance does not answer it.
items.reply: Suitcases can be stored in the lockers by the entrance, if they fit.

items.context: A ferry leaves from the harbour at 11:00. The harbour has three numbered terminals.
items.prompt: What should you ask to find the ferry?
options: Which terminal does the ferry leave from?
Which port will the ferry arrive at?
What time does the ferry leave?
How long will the crossing take?
items.explanation: The broad location and time are known. The terminal identifies the correct departure point.
items.reply: It leaves from terminal three.

items.context: Your flight arrives at 23:30. The hotel advertises a shuttle but does not list its operating hours.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether you can use it that night?
options: Will the shuttle still be running after my flight arrives?
Does the shuttle need to be booked in advance?
Does the shuttle stop at more than one hotel?
Does the shuttle fare include luggage?
items.explanation: An advertised service may not run all night. You need to check its availability after arrival.
items.reply: The last shuttle leaves at 23:00, so you will need another transfer.

items.context: A supplier says your order will arrive on Friday. Your office is staffed only until 15:00.
items.prompt: Which question helps prevent a missed delivery?
options: Can you split the order into two deliveries next week?
Can you send the invoice before the delivery?
Can you deliver before 15:00 on Friday?
Can you confirm that Friday is the delivery day?
items.explanation: The date is confirmed, but the arrival window must fit the office’s staffed hours.
items.reply: Yes. The planned delivery window is 10:00–12:00.

items.context: You ordered ten folders. The invoice lists a total price, but does not say whether delivery is included.
items.prompt: Which question clarifies the final cost?
options: Does this total include delivery?
Does the total cover all ten folders?
Can I pay the invoice by bank transfer?
Can you print the order number on the invoice?
items.explanation: The issue is an unlisted possible charge. The quantity and invoice details do not settle it.
items.reply: Delivery is separate and costs six pounds.

items.context: You received a damaged item. The seller agreed to a return but gave no instructions about the return address.
items.prompt: Which question lets you send it back correctly?
options: When should I expect a refund after the return?
Can you confirm that you have accepted the return?
Which address should I return it to?
Which delivery method was used for the original order?
items.explanation: Permission to return does not identify the correct return destination.
items.reply: Send it to the returns centre listed in the label we will email you.

items.context: An online listing says “pack of cups.” You need twenty cups, but the pack size is missing.
items.prompt: Which detail do you need before choosing a quantity?
options: How many packs can I order at once?
Are all the cups in a pack the same size?
How many cups are in one pack?
How much does each pack cost?
items.explanation: You cannot calculate the number of packs without knowing how many cups each contains.
items.reply: There are five cups in each pack, so four packs provide twenty cups.

items.context: You are ordering a replacement cable. The listing gives its length but not the type of connector.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether it can connect to your device?
options: What devices were used in the product photographs?
How long is the cable?
Is the cable sold with a storage case?
What connector is on each end?
items.explanation: A suitable length does not guarantee compatible connectors. Both ends matter.
items.reply: It has a USB-C connector at both ends.

items.context: The seller can provide the item in two sizes. You need the smaller size, but the confirmation lists only the product name.
items.prompt: What should you ask before dispatch?
options: Can you confirm that my order is for the smaller size?
Can you confirm the product name?
Can you confirm when the order will be dispatched?
Can you confirm the delivery address on my order?
items.explanation: The order’s size is unconfirmed. The product name alone cannot establish which version will arrive.
items.reply: Yes. Your order specifies the smaller size.

items.context: A delivery has arrived with one box missing. You know the total number originally ordered.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether another box is still coming?
options: Is the missing box being sent separately?
Did you send the whole order in one larger box?
Can you confirm how many boxes I ordered?
Can you confirm that the first delivery has arrived?
items.explanation: You need the status of the missing part. Some orders are split into separate deliveries.
items.reply: Yes. The last box is on a separate delivery due tomorrow.

items.context: A company offers next-day delivery. It does not state how late an order can be placed to qualify.
items.prompt: What do you need to ask?
options: Can I track a next-day delivery?
Can I change the address after placing my order?
What is the order cutoff for next-day delivery?
How much extra does next-day delivery cost?
items.explanation: A next-day promise may depend on ordering before a cutoff time.
items.reply: Place and pay for the order before 13:00 on a working day.

items.context: You need thirty printed copies by Wednesday. The printer has confirmed the quantity and completion date, but not whether you must collect them.
items.prompt: Which question clarifies the handover?
options: Will you keep a copy of the file for future orders?
Will you deliver the copies, or should I collect them?
How many copies are you printing?
On which day will printing be complete?
items.explanation: The number and date are settled. The missing detail is how the copies will reach you.
items.reply: Please collect them from the front desk after 10:00 on Wednesday.

items.context: A supplier offers a lower price for a bulk order but has not given the minimum quantity.
items.prompt: Which question helps you decide whether you qualify?
options: Can I choose several colours in a bulk order?
Will a bulk order take longer to deliver?
How many units must I order to receive that price?
How soon must I pay after placing a bulk order?
items.explanation: The minimum quantity determines whether your order qualifies for the quoted price.
items.reply: The bulk price applies to orders of at least fifty units.

items.context: Four people have agreed on a meeting date. One participant is in another time zone, and the invitation says only “9:00.”
items.prompt: What must be clarified?
options: How long is the meeting expected to last?
Which platform will we use for the meeting?
Which time zone does 9:00 refer to?
Which date have we chosen?
items.explanation: The same clock time refers to different moments in different time zones.
items.reply: The time is 9:00 in London; the calendar invitation will show your local time.

items.context: You are booking a room for twelve people. The description gives the floor area but no seating capacity.
items.prompt: Which question checks suitability?
options: Can I arrange to see the room before booking?
Can the room be booked for a whole day?
Can food be served in the room?
Can the room seat twelve people at tables?
items.explanation: Floor area alone does not establish seating for a particular arrangement.
items.reply: Yes. It seats fourteen people at tables.

items.context: A speaker will use slides. You have booked a room but have not checked its equipment.
items.prompt: Which question addresses the presentation need?
options: Is there a microphone for the speaker?
Is there space for the audience to take notes?
Is there a table where the speaker can put a laptop?
Is a working projector or screen available?
items.explanation: Slides require suitable display equipment. The other room details do not establish that.
items.reply: A screen and projector are available; bring the cable for your device.

items.context: An event starts at 18:00. Volunteers must prepare the room first, but their arrival time is not listed.
items.prompt: Which question asks for the missing instruction?
options: What time should volunteers arrive for setup?
What time does the event start?
What time will the public doors close?
What time can guests collect their tickets?
items.explanation: Setup normally needs a separate arrival time before the public start.
items.reply: Please arrive at 17:00 to set up the tables.

items.context: You are arranging lunch for a group. The number of people is known, but their food requirements are not.
items.prompt: Which question should you ask the group?
options: Would people like to sit in the same groups as last time?
Would people like to have lunch indoors or outside?
Would people like to move the lunch break to a later time?
Does anyone have food allergies or dietary requirements we should plan for?
items.explanation: Food requirements are the missing planning information. Do not infer them from the headcount.
items.reply: Two people need vegetarian meals; one also needs food without nuts.

items.context: Your team chose a date for an outing. The venue requires a deposit, but no one has been assigned to pay it.
items.prompt: Which question resolves the task gap?
options: Who will choose the date for our next outing?
Who will send directions to the venue?
Who will collect everyone’s meal choices?
Who will arrange the deposit payment?
items.explanation: The date and requirement are known. A named owner is needed for the unpaid task.
items.reply: I will arrange the payment today and send the confirmation to the group.

items.context: A workshop has an online sign-up form. You need to know whether places are still available.
items.prompt: Which question checks availability?
options: Can I register more than one person on the form?
Can I get a copy of my completed sign-up form?
Are there any places left in this workshop?
Can I save the sign-up form and finish it later?
items.explanation: An open form does not necessarily prove a place is available.
items.reply: There are three places left at the moment.

items.context: You will bring boxes to an event. The visitor entrance has stairs, and the venue information does not mention delivery access.
items.prompt: Which question helps you choose a suitable entrance?
options: Can visitors enter before the public start time?
Can the boxes stay at the venue overnight?
Can we reserve space for the boxes inside the room?
Is there step-free access for bringing in the boxes?
items.explanation: The relevant missing detail is a route suitable for carrying or wheeling boxes.
items.reply: Use the side entrance beside the ramp; it opens at 08:00.

items.context: A group agreed to finish the project this month. Several people need to hand work to one editor, but no internal hand-in date is set.
items.prompt: Which question helps the editor plan the final work?
options: By what date should we announce the completed project?
By what date should we choose the next project?
By what date should everyone send their parts to the editor?
By what date will the editor return any borrowed material?
items.explanation: The final deadline does not establish when the editor will receive the parts.
items.reply: Send all parts by the 20th so the editor has time to combine them.

items.context: You are invited to a discussion on video. The date, time, and platform are given, but you have no joining link.
items.prompt: Which request fills the practical gap?
options: Could you confirm the platform’s name?
Could you repeat the meeting date?
Could you send an agenda for the discussion?
Could you send the joining link?
items.explanation: The missing link is needed to enter this particular meeting.
items.reply: Here is the meeting link; the waiting room opens five minutes before the start.

items.context: You need a bag that fits a laptop 36 centimetres wide. A listing says “large laptop bag” without measurements.
items.prompt: Which question gives useful evidence of fit?
options: How long is the shoulder strap?
What is the width of the laptop compartment?
What is the bag’s total weight?
How many pockets does the bag have?
items.explanation: A general size label does not establish the usable compartment width.
items.reply: The laptop compartment is 38 centimetres wide.

items.context: You want to book a desk for a full working day. The price is shown per hour, but the opening hours are missing.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether the desk is available long enough?
options: Can I book the desk for someone else?
Can I pay by the hour when I arrive?
Can I change desks during the day?
What are the opening hours on the day I want?
items.explanation: You already know the price unit. Opening hours establish the available span of the day.
items.reply: The workspace is open from 08:00 to 19:00 on that day.

items.context: You need a quiet place for a confidential video meeting. A workspace offers desks in a shared room.
items.prompt: What should you ask about an alternative?
options: Do you have a private room I can book?
Can I book two desks next to each other?
Can I choose a desk beside the window?
Can I bring my own headset to a shared desk?
items.explanation: A private room addresses the stated need. More details about shared desks do not establish privacy.
items.reply: Yes. A small private meeting room can be booked by the hour.

items.context: Two courses cover the same subject and cost the same. You can attend only after 18:00.
items.prompt: Which missing detail decides whether either course fits?
options: What times do the classes meet?
How many students are in each course?
How much homework does each course include?
How many weeks does each course last?
items.explanation: Your constraint is the class time. The subject and price are already known and equal.
items.reply: Course A meets at 17:00; Course B meets at 19:00.

items.context: You need to borrow a ladder for one afternoon. A notice says equipment can be borrowed but gives no maximum loan period.
items.prompt: Which question checks whether the loan fits your plan?
options: Do I need to leave a deposit?
Can someone collect the ladder on my behalf?
How long may I keep the ladder?
Where do I collect the ladder?
items.explanation: Permission to borrow does not state how long the item may be kept.
items.reply: You may keep it until the equipment desk closes today.

items.context: You want to use an app without an internet connection during a journey. Its page lists features but not connection requirements.
items.prompt: What should you ask?
options: Which features work offline?
Which features require a paid account?
Which features can be used on a phone?
Which features save my work automatically?
items.explanation: “Offline” means without an internet connection. Ask about the functions available in that condition.
items.reply: Saved lessons work offline, but new lessons must be downloaded while connected.

items.context: You need to carry a folding table alone. Its folded size is suitable, but its weight is not listed.
items.prompt: Which question supplies the missing factor?
options: How long does it take to fold the table?
How high is the table when it is open?
How much does the table weigh?
How thick is the folded table?
items.explanation: Size and weight are different. The weight helps you judge whether you can carry it safely yourself.
items.reply: The table weighs eight kilograms.

items.context: You need a print shop to produce a bound booklet. A listing confirms printing, but says nothing about binding.
items.prompt: Which question checks the missing service?
options: Can you keep the file for a repeat order?
Can you bind the printed pages into a booklet?
Can you print on both sides of each page?
Can you print the cover in colour?
items.explanation: Printing pages and binding them are separate services. Confirm the one not listed.
items.reply: Yes. We offer simple stapled booklet binding for this page count.

items.context: You are comparing two routes. Both arrive before your appointment, but you must avoid stairs with a wheeled case.
items.prompt: Which information helps you choose?
options: Does either route offer reserved seating?
Does either route require using stairs?
Does either route cost less?
Does either route have more frequent departures?
items.explanation: The time requirement is already met. Stair access is the remaining constraint.
items.reply: Route A includes stairs at a transfer; Route B has ramps and lifts throughout.

items.context: A venue offers a group rate. Your group has eight people, but the size needed for that rate is not stated.
items.prompt: Which question establishes eligibility?
options: Can members of a group arrive separately?
Can a group pay with more than one card?
Can a group change its booking date?
What is the minimum group size for that rate?
items.explanation: You must compare your headcount with the minimum required size.
items.reply: The group rate starts at ten people, so eight does not qualify.

items.context: A colleague asks you to send “the latest file.” Two files have similar names, and both were edited today.
items.prompt: Which request avoids guessing?
options: Please confirm who should receive the file.
Please confirm the exact file name you want.
Please confirm which folder contains both files.
Please confirm whether you want a PDF or a printed copy.
items.explanation: “Latest” does not identify one file clearly here. Ask for its exact name.
items.reply: Send “Workshop-plan-final.pdf,” not the notes file.

items.context: You are told to “update the page.” The page has an old address and an old price, but the request does not say which to change.
items.prompt: Which question establishes the task’s scope?
options: How should I tell the team that the update is complete?
Which parts of the page should I update?
When should the updated page be ready?
Who should check the page after I update it?
items.explanation: Ask which content the instruction covers before changing it.
items.reply: Update both the address and the price; leave the rest unchanged.

items.context: You must hand a document to the next shift. The document is ready, but you do not know who will receive it.
items.prompt: What should you ask?
options: Should I send the document before the shift ends?
Should I keep a copy for the current shift?
Should I put the document in a folder?
Who should I give the document to?
items.explanation: The missing recipient is needed to complete the handover.
items.reply: Give it to the supervisor at the front desk.

items.context: An instruction says “send the summary to the group.” You know several groups involved in the project.
items.prompt: Which question identifies the intended recipients?
options: Should the group receive it before the meeting?
Should I include the full report with the summary?
Which group should receive the summary?
Should the summary be sent as an attachment?
items.explanation: The word “group” is unclear in this context. Ask which particular group is intended.
items.reply: Send it only to the planning group.

items.context: A customer wants “the usual amount.” This is your first time handling their order, and you cannot see earlier orders.
items.prompt: Which question avoids an unsupported assumption?
options: How many units would you like this time?
Would you like the usual amount again?
Would you like the order delivered to the usual address?
Would you like to use your usual payment method?
items.explanation: Repeating “usual” does not supply a number. Ask for the quantity explicitly.
items.reply: Please send twelve units this time.

items.context: A colleague says a draft is “fine.” You need to know whether you may publish it or should wait for another review.
items.prompt: Which question checks the next action?
options: Should I change the title before the next draft?
Should I send a copy to the person who wrote the notes?
Should I save this version alongside the earlier drafts?
May I publish it now, or is another review needed?
items.explanation: Approval of a draft’s quality may not be permission to publish. Ask about the next step.
items.reply: Please wait for the final review before publishing.

items.context: A note says “Bring the equipment tomorrow.” It gives the date but no delivery location.
items.prompt: Which question supplies the missing destination?
options: Who should I contact if my arrival is delayed?
Where should I bring the equipment?
At what time tomorrow should I bring the equipment?
Should I bring the equipment in its storage cases?
items.explanation: Knowing when to bring something does not tell you where to take it.
items.reply: Bring it to the training room on the ground floor.

items.context: You are asked to shorten a report. The reader wants it shorter but has not given a length limit.
items.prompt: Which question makes the target clearer?
options: When should I send you the revised report?
Who else should receive a copy of the shorter report?
What length should I aim for?
Which file format should I use for the shorter version?
items.explanation: A target length makes the revision more specific than “shorter.”
items.reply: Aim for two pages, including the summary.

items.context: You receive two messages about a deadline: one says Thursday and the later one says Friday. You are unsure whether the later message changes the deadline.
items.prompt: Which question resolves the conflict?
options: Does the Friday message replace the earlier Thursday deadline?
Should I send the work by email or upload it?
Should I send a reminder on Thursday?
Should I include the deadline in the report title?
items.explanation: Ask which instruction is current. The order of messages suggests a change but does not by itself explain it.
items.reply: Yes. Friday is the revised deadline; please disregard the earlier date.

items.context: You have agreed to help with an event. The organizer says “Please handle the signs,” but you do not know whether to design, print, or put them up.
items.prompt: Which question clarifies your responsibility?
options: When should all the signs be ready?
Where should the finished signs be placed?
How many copies of each sign will we need?
Should I design the signs, print them, put them up, or do all three?
items.explanation: Break the broad task into possible actions and ask which ones are yours.
items.reply: The designs are ready. Please print the signs and put them up.
